title: Free QR Code Generator — No Watermark, PNG & SVG
description: Create a free static QR code from a website link. Download PNG or SVG without an added watermark, account or API key. Your link is processed in your browser.
intro: Turn a website URL into a scannable QR code for a business card, flyer, event page or product insert. Pocket AI generates the code directly in your browser and does not add a logo, watermark or redirect service to the image.
steps: Paste a complete HTTPS or HTTP website link.
Choose a PNG size and select Create QR code.
Download PNG or scalable SVG, then scan-test the file with a phone before printing.
example: A restaurant can encode its own menu URL and place the downloaded SVG on a printed table card. The QR destination remains the original menu address, not a Pocket AI tracking link.
limits: These are static QR codes: you cannot change the encoded destination after printing. The code has no Pocket AI expiration, but the linked page must remain available. It does not shorten URLs or provide scan analytics.
question: Does the free QR code include a watermark?
answer: No. Pocket AI adds no watermark to its generated PNG or SVG QR code. Keep the white border around the code so scanners can recognize it.

title: Free Strong Password Generator — No Sign-Up
description: Generate random passwords with browser Web Crypto. Choose 8–128 characters and character types. No account or API key required; passwords are not saved.
intro: Create a fresh password for an account instead of reusing a familiar phrase. The generator uses browser cryptographic randomness and includes each selected character type rather than simply shuffling predictable words.
steps: Choose a password length between 8 and 128 characters.
Select lowercase, uppercase, digits and/or symbols.
Generate a password and save it in a trusted password manager.
example: A 20-character password with letters, digits and symbols is a useful starting point for a service that accepts that length and those characters. Generate a different password for every account.
limits: Check the receiving website's password rules. The tool does not store passwords, secure your clipboard or replace two-factor authentication. Downloaded text is not an encrypted password vault.
question: Are generated passwords uploaded?
answer: No. Password generation happens locally and this tool page does not load advertising scripts. Your device, clipboard and downloaded files still need to be protected.

title: Free Word Counter & Character Counter Online
description: Count words, characters and lines, estimate reading time, and change text case. Free browser-based word counter with Unicode support and no sign-up.
intro: Check the size of an article draft, social caption or assignment before publishing. Word and character counts update while you type, and the text controls can convert case or clean extra spacing without sending the draft to an AI provider.
steps: Paste your text into the input box.
Read word, character, line and estimated reading-time counts.
Optionally change case or clean spacing, then copy or download the result.
example: Paste a 500-word article to estimate its reading time at roughly 200 words per minute. Use the character count as a starting point for editing, rather than assuming it exactly matches every platform's limits.
limits: Word boundaries depend on language and browser segmentation. Character counts use Unicode code points, which can differ from a platform's emoji or byte-counting rules. Reading time is an estimate, not an assessment of comprehension.
question: Does this tool count non-English text?
answer: It supports Unicode input and uses browser word segmentation when available. Check unusual punctuation and languages without spaces against the rules of your intended platform.

title: Free Unit Converter — Metric & US Measurements
description: Convert miles to kilometers, pounds to kilograms, Fahrenheit to Celsius and more. Free local length, weight, volume and temperature conversion tool.
intro: Move between common metric and US measurements when planning travel, comparing specifications or checking a recipe. The category selector keeps compatible measurements together so you do not accidentally convert length into weight.
steps: Select length, weight, volume or temperature.
Enter a value and choose the source and destination units.
Convert and review the labeled result before using it.
example: One mile equals 1.609344 kilometers, while 32 degrees Fahrenheit equals 0 degrees Celsius. These are different formulas: temperature conversion includes an offset rather than a simple ratio.
limits: Volume uses US customary gallons, fluid ounces and cups, not Imperial measures. Displayed results are rounded. Temperatures below absolute zero are rejected.
question: Which cup and gallon definitions are used?
answer: The tool uses US customary units, including a US cup of approximately 236.588 mL and a US gallon of 3.785411784 L. Check regional recipe definitions before converting.

title: Free Percentage Calculator — Change, Share & Percent
description: Calculate a percentage of a number, one number as a percentage of another, or percentage change. Free calculator with clear formulas and no account.
intro: Answer common percentage questions without rearranging formulas by hand. Choose whether you need a part of a total, a share expressed as a percent, or a change between two values.
steps: Select the calculation type.
Enter A and B according to the displayed question.
Calculate and check whether the result is a number or a percentage.
example: For “What is A% of B?”, enter 15 and 200 to get 30. For change from 100 to 125, choose percentage change to get 25%.
limits: Percentage change from zero is undefined. This calculator defines change as (B − A) divided by the absolute value of A, multiplied by 100. Financial reporting conventions for negative starting values can differ.
question: Can it calculate a discount?
answer: Yes. Calculate the discount percentage of the original price to find the amount saved, then subtract that amount from the price. This is not a tax-inclusive checkout calculator.

title: Free UTM Link Builder — Campaign URL Generator
description: Build campaign URLs with UTM source, medium, campaign, term and content. Preserve existing parameters and fragments. No account needed; not a link shortener.
intro: Create consistent tracking links for newsletters, social posts and campaigns. The builder adds standard UTM parameters to your destination URL so a compatible analytics setup can identify the traffic source.
steps: Enter the complete destination URL.
Fill in source, medium and campaign; optionally add term and content.
Generate the URL and use it in the relevant campaign.
example: An email campaign can use source=newsletter, medium=email and campaign=summer_launch. Use content=hero_button to distinguish a header button from a footer link in the same message.
limits: UTM links are longer tracking URLs, not shortened links. The tool does not collect analytics itself. Existing non-UTM parameters and URL fragments are preserved; blank optional UTM fields remove those parameters.
question: Will this shorten my website link?
answer: No. This is a campaign URL builder, not a shortener. It adds tracking parameters. Attribution only works if the destination's analytics software records and interprets them.

title: Free JSON Formatter, Validator & Minifier
description: Format JSON with two-space indentation, validate syntax, or minify JSON locally. Free browser tool with readable errors and no upload required.
intro: Turn compact JSON into a readable structure or remove unnecessary formatting for a smaller text payload. The tool uses strict JSON parsing, so it can identify syntax mistakes before data is passed to another system.
steps: Paste a JSON object, array or other valid JSON value.
Choose pretty print or minify.
Format the data; correct any syntax error, then copy or download the result.
example: The input {"name":"Pocket","active":true} becomes an indented object in pretty-print mode. Minify mode produces compact JSON without changing parsed values.
limits: Comments and trailing commas are not accepted. Input is limited to 200,000 characters. JavaScript numeric precision applies: quote large numeric IDs if their exact digits must be preserved.
question: Is JSON uploaded to a server?
answer: No. Formatting is performed in your browser. Avoid sharing a copied result if it contains secrets, and remember that formatting is not data anonymization.

title: Free Base64 Encoder & Decoder — UTF-8 Text
description: Encode Unicode text to Base64 or decode valid padded Base64 into UTF-8. A free local text tool with no sign-up. Base64 is not encryption.
intro: Convert text into a Base64 representation when an integration expects encoded text, or inspect a UTF-8 message that is already encoded. Unicode handling preserves non-English characters rather than treating each character as one byte.
steps: Paste plain text or an encoded Base64 string.
Choose Encode or Decode.
Convert the input and copy the result, checking that the text is what you expect.
example: A message containing বাংলা or an emoji can be encoded and decoded without losing those characters. This is useful for text-oriented API payloads and debugging.
limits: This workflow supports UTF-8 text, not arbitrary binary files. Decoding expects valid padded Base64 and rejects invalid UTF-8. Base64 provides no confidentiality.
question: Can I protect a password with Base64?
answer: No. Anyone can reverse Base64 without a secret key. Use established encryption and a password manager instead of treating encoding as security.

title: Free URL Encoder & Decoder — URL Components
description: Encode or decode URL components with Unicode support. Handle spaces, slashes and special characters in a free browser tool without sending text to a server.
intro: Prepare a single value for use in a URL component or read a percent-encoded value during debugging. Component encoding helps distinguish data from characters that normally have special meaning in a URL.
steps: Paste the component value or percent-encoded text.
Choose Encode or Decode.
Convert and copy the result into the appropriate URL field.
example: A query value such as “summer sale & gifts” needs encoded spaces and an encoded ampersand when inserted as one parameter. This prevents the ampersand from being treated as a separator.
limits: This tool encodes a component, not an entire navigable website URL. It does not shorten links. Literal plus signs remain plus signs during decoding; this is not form-urlencoded decoding.
question: Why does my complete URL get encoded slashes?
answer: Component encoding treats slashes and punctuation as data. Use the result as a component value, not as a replacement for an entire URL.

title: YouTube Thumbnail Downloader — Available Image Sizes
description: Find available YouTube thumbnail sizes from a video URL or ID. Download a JPG when allowed, or open the image to save it. No account required.
intro: Find the public thumbnail images associated with a YouTube video without manually constructing image URLs. The tool checks maximum, standard and high-quality variants and shows available dimensions.
steps: Paste a YouTube watch, Shorts, live, embed or short-link URL.
Find thumbnails and wait for the resolution checks.
Download an available JPG or use Open image if the browser blocks direct downloading.
example: Use your own video's YouTube link to retrieve a thumbnail for a portfolio entry. Some videos have a high-quality image but no maximum-resolution variant.
limits: This contacts YouTube's image hosts. Network restrictions, deleted or private videos and missing sizes can prevent results. A publicly accessible thumbnail is not a license to reuse someone else's work.
question: Why is the highest-resolution thumbnail unavailable?
answer: Not every video has every image size. Choose another available variant. If all images are blocked, check network access and try the tool on the live site.

title: YouTube Tag Generator — Free Local Suggestions & AI Mode
description: Build YouTube keyword tag suggestions from your topic. Use free local rules or optional AI generation with a working provider. No ranking guarantees.
intro: Start a relevant tag list from your video's actual topic, audience and vocabulary. Local mode produces keyword suggestions using rules; optional AI mode can generate alternatives when this deployment has a working provider.
steps: Describe your video topic and intended audience.
Choose local suggestions or the optional AI mode.
Review the suggested tags, remove irrelevant terms and copy the final list.
example: For a home-office productivity tutorial, start with the core topic and the specific activity demonstrated. Do not add unrelated celebrity or trending tags just to attract traffic.
limits: Local suggestions are not AI output, search-volume research or extracted competitor tags. AI mode depends on credentials, connectivity and quota. Tags alone do not guarantee views or rankings.
question: Can I use it without an AI API key?
answer: Yes, in local mode. That mode uses deterministic keyword rules. For model-generated suggestions, switch to AI mode only after a server-side provider is configured and reachable.

title: Free English Readability Checker — Flesch & Grade Level
description: Estimate English Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch–Kincaid Grade, plus word count and reading time. Free local checker with clearly stated limitations.
intro: Get a rough signal of how demanding an English draft may be for a reader. Readability formulas use word, sentence and syllable estimates; they can help identify dense prose but cannot judge accuracy or usefulness.
steps: Paste a representative passage of English prose.
Run the readability check.
Review the estimated scores and edit long or unclear sentences in context.
example: Compare a long paragraph full of specialist terminology with a version that explains the same idea using shorter sentences. Use the scores alongside feedback from actual readers.
limits: Syllables and sentence boundaries are heuristic. Names, abbreviations, very short texts and non-English writing can produce misleading scores. Grade level refers to an approximate US school-grade formula.
question: Does a high reading-ease score mean the article is good?
answer: No. It suggests simpler surface language under the formula. It does not measure factual accuracy, structure, empathy, relevance or whether readers understand the material.

title: AI Prompt Generator & Refiner — Free Local Templates
description: Build a reusable prompt with task, audience, tone, format and constraints. Free local template mode; optional AI refinement needs a working provider.
intro: Replace an underspecified request with a structured prompt that tells an assistant what to do, for whom and in what format. Start locally or ask a configured AI provider to refine your draft without executing the underlying task.
steps: Describe the task or paste an existing prompt.
Add audience, tone, output format and useful constraints.
Generate a local template or select AI refinement, then review the prompt before using it.
example: Instead of “write marketing copy,” specify a welcome email for new software users, a concise friendly tone, a clear next action and no unsupported claims.
limits: A template is not a model response and does not ensure a particular assistant will follow every instruction. AI mode sends the entered text to the server and provider; exclude secrets and private client data.
question: Is local prompt generation actually AI?
answer: No. Local mode assembles an explicit reusable template. It is labeled separately from AI refinement so you can choose between an API-free workflow and a live provider request.

title: Free Freelancer Hourly Rate Calculator
description: Estimate a freelance hourly rate from annual take-home goals, business expenses, billable hours and a tax reserve. Free planning calculator, no account.
intro: Translate an annual income goal into an hourly rate based on the time you can realistically bill. Non-billable work, holidays and expenses matter: dividing a salary by every working hour can understate the rate needed.
steps: Enter your desired annual take-home income and business expenses.
Set working weeks, billable hours per week and a flat tax reserve percentage.
Calculate a suggested rate and compare it with your project scope and market.
example: With 60,000 take-home income, 10,000 expenses, a 25% reserve and 1,500 annual billable hours, the estimated rate is 60 in your selected currency.
limits: The reserve is modeled as a flat percentage of profit. This does not calculate national taxes, VAT, benefits or market demand. All entered amounts must use the same currency.
question: Should I enter every hour I work?
answer: Use billable hours, not total time at your desk. Sales, bookkeeping, training and unpaid administration reduce the hours available to invoice.

title: Freelancer Tax Reserve Calculator — Flat-Rate Estimate
description: Estimate a freelance tax reserve from revenue, expenses and your chosen effective rate. Free calculator with clear assumptions, not a tax-filing service.
intro: Set aside an estimated amount from freelance profit using a rate you choose with appropriate advice. This simple model helps with cash-flow planning without pretending to know your country, filing status or deductions.
steps: Enter revenue and estimated deductible expenses for the same period.
Choose an effective tax reserve percentage.
Review pre-tax profit, reserved tax and remaining income.
example: For revenue of 10,000 and expenses of 2,000, profit is 8,000. At a 25% reserve rate, the tool sets aside 2,000 and shows 6,000 remaining.
limits: This is not a US, UK or other country's tax return calculator. It omits brackets, credits, social contributions and VAT. Loss scenarios are not modeled. Seek qualified advice when choosing the rate.
question: Does this calculate my exact tax bill?
answer: No. It applies the flat rate you enter to estimated profit. Actual liability depends on jurisdiction and personal circumstances.

title: Free Mortgage Calculator — Monthly Payment Estimate
description: Estimate fixed-rate mortgage principal and interest, total loan payments and monthly extras. Choose a currency and review transparent assumptions.
intro: Explore how price, down payment, interest rate and term affect a fixed-rate mortgage payment. The calculator separates principal and interest from optional monthly costs so you can see what is included.
steps: Enter property price and down payment in the same currency.
Set the nominal annual rate and loan term.
Add monthly taxes, insurance or other costs if needed, then calculate.
example: A larger down payment reduces the financed principal. Shortening the term generally increases the monthly principal-and-interest payment while reducing total interest, assuming the same fixed rate.
limits: This is an amortization estimate, not a lender quote. It does not independently calculate closing costs, mortgage insurance, property tax or HOA fees. Extras entered are excluded from total loan repayments.
question: Is the interest rate the same as lender APR?
answer: Not necessarily. This model divides a nominal annual interest rate by 12. Lender APR may include fees and use rules that the calculator does not model.

title: Free Loan Calculator — Monthly Payments & Interest
description: Calculate fixed-rate monthly loan payments, total repayment and interest. Free browser calculator with a zero-interest case and no sign-up.
intro: Compare repayment estimates for a personal, vehicle or other fixed-rate installment loan. The calculator uses equal monthly payments over the entered term and shows the difference between borrowed principal and interest.
steps: Enter the loan amount and nominal annual interest rate.
Choose the repayment term in years.
Calculate monthly payment, total payments and total interest.
example: A 1,200 loan with zero interest over one year has a monthly payment of 100. At positive interest rates, part of each payment covers interest on the outstanding balance.
limits: Fees, irregular payment dates, early repayments and changing rates are not modeled. The rate is divided into monthly periods. Your lender's exact schedule may differ.
question: Can I compare different loan terms?
answer: Yes. Change the term while keeping principal and rate the same, then compare monthly payment and total interest. Consider affordability and all real fees before deciding.

title: Free Compound Interest Calculator — Monthly Contributions
description: Estimate a future balance with monthly compounding and regular contributions. View contributions and hypothetical growth without an account.
intro: Explore a savings scenario using a starting balance, regular deposits and a constant assumed rate. Separating contributions from growth helps you understand how much of the projected balance comes from your own money.
steps: Enter a starting balance and monthly contribution.
Set a nominal annual return and time period.
Review future balance, total contributions and estimated growth.
example: At a zero return, an initial 1,000 plus twelve monthly contributions of 100 produces 2,200. A positive assumed return adds growth through monthly compounding.
limits: Contributions are added at the end of each month. The model excludes taxes, fees, inflation, volatility and withdrawals. Returns are hypothetical rather than forecasts or guarantees.
question: When are the monthly deposits invested?
answer: At each month end in this model. Beginning-of-month contributions would have more time to earn returns and can produce a different result.

title: Free Profit Margin Calculator — SaaS & E-commerce
description: Calculate profit, margin and markup for monthly SaaS revenue or an e-commerce order. Include direct costs, fees and overhead in a free local calculator.
intro: Keep margin and markup distinct when reviewing a product or subscription business. Margin measures profit relative to revenue; markup measures profit relative to costs. Enter all costs relevant to the measure you want.
steps: Choose monthly SaaS or per-order e-commerce as the basis.
Enter revenue, direct costs, fees and allocated overhead.
Calculate profit, margin percentage and markup.
example: Revenue of 100 with total entered costs of 60 gives profit of 40, a 40% margin and approximately 66.67% markup. These percentages are not interchangeable.
limits: The tool cannot know costs you omit. It does not independently calculate tax, churn, customer acquisition cost or refunds. Zero cost makes markup undefined; negative profit indicates a loss.
question: Does the result show gross or net margin?
answer: That depends on which costs you include. Enter direct costs for a gross-style measure or all relevant allocated costs for a more comprehensive estimate, and label your result accordingly.

title: Free WebP & AVIF Converter — No Added Watermark
description: Convert still images to WebP or AVIF locally with quality and size controls. No added watermark or upload required; input and browser limits apply.
intro: Create modern image formats for a website or digital project without uploading the source image. WebP conversion uses browser canvas; AVIF conversion uses a self-hosted WebAssembly encoder in a worker.
steps: Choose a supported PNG, JPEG, WebP or AVIF input image.
Select WebP or AVIF, quality and maximum output dimension.
Convert, compare file sizes and download the result.
example: Convert a product photo to WebP for a web page, then compare its appearance and file size with AVIF at a similar quality. A lower numerical quality is not a guarantee of an acceptable visual result.
limits: Maximum input is 15 MB and 16 megapixels; output dimensions are capped at 2048 pixels per side. Only a still image is exported; animation and most metadata are not preserved. Smaller files are not guaranteed.
question: Does the converter remove an existing watermark?
answer: No. It adds no Pocket AI watermark, but does not remove marks already present in the pixels. Respect image ownership and compare the converted image before publishing.

title: Free PDF Merger — Combine Files Without Uploading
description: Merge PDFs in a chosen order directly in your browser. No added watermark or account required. Review file-size, page and document-feature limits.
intro: Combine several PDF documents into one downloadable file while keeping source files on your device. The visible file list lets you move documents up or down before merging, rather than relying on filename order.
steps: Select the PDFs you want to combine.
Use the up/down controls to arrange the document order.
Merge, download and inspect the resulting PDF before sharing it.
example: Combine a proposal and supporting appendix into one delivery file. Place the proposal first, then verify that the appendix starts on the expected page after downloading.
limits: Limits are 10 files, 20 MB total input and 500 pages. Encrypted PDFs are unsupported. Rewriting may affect forms, signatures, bookmarks and accessibility structure; keep originals.
question: Does merging preserve digital signatures?
answer: Do not assume so. Combining or rewriting signed documents can invalidate signatures. Preserve original signed files and follow the recipient's document requirements.

title: Free PDF Splitter — Extract Selected Pages Locally
description: Extract PDF pages or ranges into a new file in your browser. No upload or added watermark. Choose ranges such as 1–3, 5 and download selected pages.
intro: Create a smaller selection of pages when you do not need to share an entire document. Enter page numbers or ranges, and the tool creates one new PDF containing the requested pages.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF.
Enter page numbers or ranges, such as 1-3, 5.
Extract, download and inspect the selected-page PDF.
example: From a ten-page report, choose 1, 8-10 to create a file with the introduction and closing section. Repeated page numbers are included only once.
limits: This extracts one file per run, not a ZIP containing one file for every page. Repeat with another selection to create multiple parts. Limits include 20 MB and 500 pages; document features may not survive rewriting.
question: Are page numbers zero-based?
answer: No. Enter 1 for the first page. The tool validates ranges against the document's actual page count and rejects descending or out-of-range selections.

title: Free PDF Compressor — Best-Effort Local Optimization
description: Try structural PDF optimization without uploading your document. Download a smaller result when possible, or the unchanged original when no savings are found.
intro: Try reducing structural PDF overhead using compressed object streams. This method is useful for some documents, but it is different from reducing image resolution or aggressively recompressing scanned pages.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF within the input limits.
Run the optimizer and read the reported size savings.
Download the result or the unchanged original when no smaller output is found.
example: A PDF written with uncompressed structural objects may shrink after optimization. An already-optimized scan may not, because most of its size can be embedded images.
limits: There is no guaranteed compression ratio. The tool does not downsample images. Rewriting can affect signatures, forms or other document structure; keep your original and inspect the output.
question: Why did my PDF not get smaller?
answer: It may already be optimized, or its size may mostly come from image data this workflow does not recompress. The tool then offers the original unchanged rather than claiming fake savings.
